title: The Dire Dawa Hotel Room Where Dahabshiil's Transfers Began
conflicts: Duale's translated interview dates the SNM attack on Burao to May 1987 in one place and May 1988 in another; HRW (1989) and all other sources say May 1988, which the story uses. Refugee totals differ (HRW 450,000 to Ethiopia/Djibouti/Kenya; GOOD 800,000; Somaliland Current about half a million), so none is given. GOOD has Duale settling in Dire Dawa with his family and using bike messengers; his own account has him alone and delivering in person, which the story follows. Warehouse count (three vs five) and staff figures (1,000 to 10,000) conflict and are omitted.
notes: Slate year 1991 corrected to August 1988 and the country to Ethiopia (Dire Dawa), where Duale says the remittance business began; arc set to change-of-direction. Main source is Ahmed I. Samatar's 2019 interview with Duale (Bildhaan vol. 21, 2021), translated from Somali; the story attributes to him. Later regulatory scrutiny of Somali remittances is deliberately left out as outside the episode.
